preamble: Place assimilation of the moraic nasal to a following alveolar consonant (/t, d, ts, dz, n/), yielding the lamino-alveolar nasal [n]. The moraic nasal /N/ (ん) of Japanese is phonologically placeless and is conventionally written /ɴ/ after its traditional pre-pausal description, though real-time MRI work (Maekawa 2023) shows that even utterance-final /N/ ranges from the hard palate to the uvula depending on the preceding vowel. No language outside Japonic is documented with a uvular nasal that assimilates in this way; elsewhere [ɴ] is usually itself an allophone of /n/ or /ŋ/ before uvulars.

examples.note: /ɴ/ before the alveolar stop /t/ surfaces as [n].
/ɴ/ before /n/ yields a long alveolar nasal.
The first /ɴ/ assimilates to the following /n/; the word-final one keeps its pre-pausal uvular realization.
